children.translated_text: <s>Ahorātravratakathā</s> (The Narrative of the Day-and-Night Vow)
<s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to the glorious <s>Dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality)!
Pure as the sky, free from conceptual elaboration, the abode of qualities,
constituted of the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), tranquil — homage to that one whose essence is the <s>stūpa</s>! [<s>Avk</s> 1]

children.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam ekasmin samaye buddho bhagavāñ chrāvastyāṃ viharati sma jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdham anekair devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragaiḥ sthavirabhikṣuvītarāgasaṃghair bodhisattvaśatasahasraiḥ saṃbahulaiś ca śrāvakair daśabhir lokapālaiś caturmahārājakāyikair anekaiś caturvarṇakair manuṣyair anekaśatasahasraiḥ parivāraiḥ parivṛtaiḥ / tasmin sabhāmaṇḍale sarve dharmaśravaṇikā lokā bhagavantam abhivīkṣya caityavratakathām anudhyāyantaḥ samāsthitāḥ / atha khalu subhūtiḥ sthaviraḥ svāsanāt samutthāyaikāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya savyajānubimbaṃ bhuvi sthāpya bhagavantaṃ praṇamyaitad avocat /
children.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, in the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, together with a great assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s>, with numerous <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s>, with assemblies of elder <s>bhikṣus</s> free from passion, with hundreds of thousands of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, with many <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers), with the ten world-protectors, with the <s>Caturmahārājakāyika</s> (Four Great King) deities, with numerous people of the four classes, and with retinues of many hundreds of thousands. In that assembly hall, all the beings who had come to hear the <s>Dharma</s>, gazing upon the <s>Bhagavān</s>, were seated contemplating the narrative of the <s>caitya</s> (shrine) observance. Then the elder <s>Subhūti</s>, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, circumambulating three times, placing his right knee on the ground, bowing to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, spoke thus:
O Lord, at what time does the day-and-night vow (<s>ahorātravrata</s>) come into effect?

children.text: tadvidhiṃ ca kathaṃ brūhi tat sarvaṃ jagatāṃ prabho || 2 ||
children.translated_text: And tell its procedure — all of that, O Lord of beings! [<s>Avk</s> 2]
The <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

children.text: sādhu sādhu subhūte tvaṃ śṛṇu sattvānukampaka /
children.translated_text: Well done, well done, <s>Subhūti</s>! Listen, O compassionate one toward beings!
I shall teach the day-and-night vow, which is perpetual, and its procedure. [<s>Avk</s> 3]
There was in [the land of] <s>Pūrvavideha</s> a city named <s>Gandhavatī</s>,
and in it, a king of great splendor, <s>Indrapṛṣṭha</s>, the great lord. [<s>Avk</s> 4]
He, having arranged an assembly in the inner court, to <s>Vasubandhu</s>, the teacher of the world,
bowing and quickly rising, asked according to the prescribed manner, with joy: [<s>Avk</s> 5]

children.text: śrotum icchāmi tat sarvaṃ yad vratānāṃ samuttamam /
children.translated_text: I wish to hear all that — which is the supreme among vows,
by the power of whose merit beings attain perfect bliss. [<s>Avk</s> 6]
Speak all of that, O wise one, O compassionate one toward all beings!
And this world, beset by evil deeds, should be protected by you. [<s>Avk</s> 7]
<s>Vasubandhu</s> said:

children.text: śṛṇu rājan mayā khyātaṃ vratānāṃ vratam uttamam /
children.translated_text: Listen, O king, to what I shall declare — the supreme vow among vows,
the day-and-night vow (<s>ahorātravrata</s>), formerly proclaimed by [the <s>Buddha</s>] <s>Vipaśyin</s>. [<s>Avk</s> 8]
On the full moon of <s>Āśvina</s> (September-October), one should perform this vow of great prosperity,

children.text: caityaṃ saṃpūjayec chuddhaḥ ṣoḍaśair vidhibhis tathā || 9 ||
children.translated_text: and, being pure, one should worship the <s>caitya</s> with sixteen ritual procedures. [<s>Avk</s> 9]
After the meal on the thirteenth [day], one should perform the cleaning of teeth and the like;
on the fourteenth, one should especially have the barbering done. [<s>Avk</s> 10]

children.text: snānaṃ kṛtvā ca tīrtheṣu śucivastrāvṛtaḥ sudhīḥ /
children.translated_text: Having bathed at sacred bathing-places, the wise one, clad in clean garments,

children.text: madhyāhne pūjayec caityaṃ pradīpaṃ ca pradāpayet || 11 ||
children.translated_text: should worship the <s>caitya</s> at midday and should light a lamp. [<s>Avk</s> 11]

children.text: sūrye ṣaṣṭhagate bhāge prāśayec ca kṣīrodanam /
children.translated_text: When the sun has reached its sixth portion, one should eat rice with milk;

children.text: punar śaucādikaṃ kṛtvā dharmaṃ ca śruṇuyān mudā || 12 ||
children.translated_text: then, having performed purification and the like, one should listen to the <s>Dharma</s> with joy. [<s>Avk</s> 12]

children.text: pratyūṣe pūrṇamāsyāṃ tu snātvā vrataṃ samārabhet /
children.translated_text: At dawn on the full moon day, having bathed, one should commence the vow;
first, having cleaned the ground, one should prepare the <s>dharmaśālā</s> (hall of <s>Dharma</s>). [<s>Avk</s> 13]
With fragrant and cool waters, one should bathe the excellent <s>caitya</s>;
with cow's milk and five jewels, one should anoint it with stone-ash paste. [<s>Avk</s> 14]

children.text: catvāraś ca dhvajāḥ sthāpyā vitānaṃ saha cāmaraiḥ /
children.translated_text: Four banners should be erected, along with a canopy and fly-whisks;

children.text: digmālā vividhaiḥ puṣpair lambayec ca jinālaye || 15 ||
children.translated_text: garlands in the [four] directions, of various flowers, should be hung in the <s>Jina's</s> (Victor's) abode. [<s>Avk</s> 15]

children.text: tadanu vratam ārabhya guruṃ vajradharaṃ namet /
children.translated_text: Then, having commenced the vow, one should bow to the teacher <s>Vajradhara</s>;
having taken refuge in the Three Jewels, one should meditate upon the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality). [<s>Avk</s> 16]
The <s>caitya</s>, constituted of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, the supreme abode of the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors),
proclaimed as the primordially awakened (<s>anādibuddha</s>), the dwelling of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>,
the abode of all deities — having worshipped the <s>caitya</s>, one should practice the vow. [<s>Avk</s> 17]
Seated on a thousand-petaled lotus, radiant as the orb of the moon,
red, born from the syllable <s>BHOḤ</s>, with four faces, resplendent, [<s>Avk</s> 18]
the primary face red-white, the southern face saffron-red,
the western face lotus-red, the northern face yellow-red, [<s>Avk</s> 19]
with eight arms, resplendent, <s>Vāgīśvara</s> (Lord of Speech), the teacher of the world,
holding bow and arrow with two [hands], holding noose and goad likewise,
and the book of <s>Prajñā</s> (Wisdom), a sword, and a <s>vajra</s>-bell with the other [hands]. [<s>Avk</s> 20]
Endowed with all essences, seated in the graceful posture (<s>lalitāsana</s>),
adorned with divine ornaments, wearing a crown of five <s>Buddhas</s>. [<s>Avk</s> 21]
<s>Vāgīśvara</s>, the supremely white, established in all <s>dharmas</s> —

children.text: evaṃ svahṛdi saṃbhāvya puraḥ sthāpya prapūjayet || 22 ||
children.translated_text: having thus visualized [Him] in one's own heart, having placed [Him] before [oneself], one should worship [Him]. [<s>Avk</s> 22]
Having offered water for the feet, water for sipping, and the <s>arghya</s> offering, with devotion,
with aquatic and terrestrial flowers, with the five fragrances, [<s>Avk</s> 23]

children.text: sāṃyojikaiḥ sugandhaiś ca sudhūpair dhūpanais tathā /
children.translated_text: with composite fragrances, and with fine incense and fumigations,
with lamps fed with ghee, and with divine food-offerings, [<s>Avk</s> 24]
with parasols, banners, and flags, with dance, song, and sweet music,
with fruits, roots, and leaves, with betel nut and betel leaf, [<s>Avk</s> 25]
with various medicinal herbs, both divine and human,
with <s>kunda</s> flowers, unbroken grains, <s>dūrvā</s> grass, parched rice, and five jewels, [<s>Avk</s> 26]
with milk and a conch-shell offering of fine flowers — one should present [these] to the excellent <s>caitya</s>;

children.text: dhāraṇīṃ caiva stotraṃ ca paṭhed gītaṃ ca gāyayet || 27 ||
children.translated_text: one should recite <s>dhāraṇīs</s> (spells) and hymns, and should sing songs. [<s>Avk</s> 27]
One should joyfully perform a thousand circumambulations,

children.text: rātriṃ divā susaṃpūrṇaṃ pracarec ca pradakṣiṇām || 28 ||
children.translated_text: and throughout the night and day, one should completely carry out the circumambulation. [<s>Avk</s> 28]

children.text: yatra devālaye tīrthe sarvān devān prapūjayet /
hīnajātiprasaṅgaṃ ca sparśanaṃ naiva kārayet // Avk_29 /
children.translated_text: one should not engage in contact with persons of low birth. [<s>Avk</s> 29]
If touched, one should proceed after bathing and should purify [oneself] with the five products of the cow (<s>pañcagavya</s>);

children.text: asparśe 'pi caret snānaṃ trisaṃdhyaṃ saṃcared vratī || 30 ||
children.translated_text: even without touching, one should bathe, and the observer of the vow should perform [the observance] at the three junctions [of the day]. [<s>Avk</s> 30]
In whatever temple, at whatever sacred site, one should worship all the deities;

children.text:
{CD add the following after 'śodhayet' :
śucikrama tathā dharmam uttamam ahorātravrataṃ //
children.translated_text:
{Alternative reading after 'should purify':
The pure procedure — the supreme <s>Dharma</s>, the day-and-night vow.
When the [auspicious] day increases, it should not be performed; even when able, one should perform [it properly].

children.text:
nidrāsevitaṃ nidrāṃ kṛtvā viśrāmasevitaṃ viśrāmaṃ kṛtvā rājan
tathā vrataṃ kārayed doṣakam 'sti tasmān na kārayet // Avk_30* //}
children.translated_text:
O king, having rested after sleep, having rested after repose,
if one performs the vow thus, there is fault — therefore one should not perform [it so]. [<s>Avk</s> 30*]}

children.text: ahorātraṃ susaṃpūrṇaṃ na nidrāṃ kārayed vratī /
children.translated_text: For the full day and night, the observer of the vow should not sleep;
absorbed in meditation on the <s>caitya</s>, one should proceed reciting and reading hymns. [<s>Avk</s> 31]
With great enthusiasm in various songs, with dances and sweet-sounding musical instruments,
with exclamations of '<s>hāhā</s>' and joyful exultation, one should perform the circumambulation. [<s>Avk</s> 32]

children.text: viśrāmaṃ vā na kuryāc ca khedaṃ vā vratamānasaḥ /
children.translated_text: One should not take rest, nor [feel] weariness, with a mind [fixed] on the vow;

children.text: ahorātre susaṃpūrṇe prātaḥ snātvā vrataṃ caret || 33 ||
children.translated_text: when the full day and night are completed, having bathed in the morning, one should conclude the vow. [<s>Avk</s> 33]
Having performed worship of the <s>caitya</s> as prescribed, one should perform worship of the guru;

children.text: annaṃ vastraṃ suvarṇaṃ ca vrīhiratnāni bhūṣitān || 34 ||
children.translated_text: food, cloth, gold, rice, jewels, and ornaments [<s>Avk</s> 34]
should be given to the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) according to one's ability, with great devotion;

children.text: yajñaṃ kuryāt tato vajrī vrataṃ pūrṇaṃ prapūrayet || 35 ||
children.translated_text: then the <s>vajra</s>-holder should perform the sacrifice and bring the vow to completion. [<s>Avk</s> 35]

children.text: abhiṣekaṃ tato dattvā pañcasūtraṃ ghaṭaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: Then, having given the consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>), the five threads, and the pot (<s>ghaṭa</s>),
having given [these] individually to each observer of the vow, one should bestow the blessing. [<s>Avk</s> 36]
Having performed the worship of the <s>Kaumārī</s> (virgin), one should partake of the remaining food,
combined with yogurt and sugar — the five nectars (<s>pañcāmṛta</s>), an excellent repast. [<s>Avk</s> 37]

children.text: gaṇacakraṃ tataḥ kuryād vidhijñas tadvidhiṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: Then one should perform the <s>gaṇacakra</s> (communal feast), the knower of the procedure, according to the prescribed method;

children.text: ity evaṃ vratarājaṃ tad yaḥ kuryāc chuddhamānasaḥ || 38 ||
children.translated_text: thus, whoever performs this king of vows with a pure mind, [<s>Avk</s> 38]
having enjoyed abundant wealth, endowed with all happiness,
obtains happiness in the next life, in the world of <s>Dharma</s>, O king! [<s>Avk</s> 39]
<s>Indrapṛṣṭha</s> said:

children.text: bhagavan sarvavin nātha punar vaktuṃ tvam arhasi /
children.translated_text: O <s>Bhagavān</s>, omniscient lord, please speak again!

children.text: saṃsāre bahudhā jātis teṣāṃ pracāraṇaṃ katham || 40 ||
children.translated_text: In <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) there are many births — how should the practice proceed for them? [<s>Avk</s> 40]

children.text: vratapūjāphalaṃ sarvaṃ kālaṃ ca samayaṃ dinam /
children.translated_text: The fruit of the vow-worship, all of it — the time, the occasion, the day,

children.text: kutra sthāne vrataṃ kāryaṃ tat sarvaṃ vada sāṃpratam || 41 ||
children.translated_text: in what place should the vow be performed? Tell all of that now! [<s>Avk</s> 41]
<s>Vasubandhu</s> said:

children.text: śṛṇu rājan mahābhāga saṃkṣepād gaditaṃ mayā /
children.translated_text: Listen, O greatly fortunate king, to what I tell you in brief:
At <s>Svayambhū</s> especially, merit is supremely great. [<s>Avk</s> 42]
In the absence of that, in one's own land, at a permanent, excellent <s>caitya</s>;
in the absence of that, having made [a <s>caitya</s>] oneself or having had it made by others, [<s>Avk</s> 43]

children.text: suvarṇena kṛte vāpi ratnaiś cānyaiś ca dhātubhiḥ /
children.translated_text: whether made of gold, or of jewels and other metals,
or of stone, wood, brick, or clay, [<s>Avk</s> 44]
or of a ball of sand and rice, or on painted cloth,
at a temple, at a river-bank, at a sacred site, on meritorious ground — [<s>Avk</s> 45]
having first purified the <s>dharmaśālā</s> (hall of <s>Dharma</s>), one should perform the vow according to the prescribed procedure.
With flowers, unbroken rice, fragrances, and water, at the foremost of <s>caityas</s> — ‖ 46 ‖

children.text: arghaṃ dadyād raveḥ pūrvaṃ puṣpaṃ kṣipet salājakam /
children.translated_text: One should offer the <s>argha</s> (water offering) first to the sun, and cast flowers along with parched grain.
One should draw the <s>maṇḍala</s> of the five deities with cow-dung water — ‖ 47 ‖
With syllables that are unfailing, one should sprinkle the observers of the vow well with water.
With <s>mantras</s> whose syllables end in the <s>ha</s>-group, [the power] is established upon the head of the vow-observer — ‖ 48 ‖

children.text: oṃ āḥ hūm iti mantreṇa diśobandhaṃ satarjitam /
children.translated_text: With the <s>mantra</s> '<s>Oṃ Āḥ Hūṃ</s>,' one should perform the binding of the directions along with the threatening gesture.

children.text: aṅganyāsaṃ karanyāsaṃ kṛtvā guruṃ ca vandayet || 49 ||
children.translated_text: Having performed <s>aṅganyāsa</s> (placing [mantras] on the limbs) and <s>karanyāsa</s> (placing [mantras] on the hands), one should salute the <s>guru</s> — ‖ 49 ‖
Holding flowers and unbroken rice in the hand, one should cast three handfuls of flowers.
Arisen from the five elements, seated upon the lotus pericarp — ‖ 50 ‖
One should invoke the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> (essence of reality), the resplendent Lord of Speech (<s>Vāgīśvara</s>).
Having drawn [him] forth in the form of wisdom, having established [him], one should worship [him] at the appointed time — ‖ 51 ‖

children.text: āvāhayāmi tvaṃ nātha tiṣṭha tatra manohare /
children.translated_text: I invoke you, O Lord; remain there, O delightful one.

children.text: sthiro bhava sadā mā gāḥ sāṃnidhyaṃ kuru sthāvare || 52 ||
children.translated_text: Be steadfast, never depart; make your presence abide in this sacred place — ‖ 52 ‖
With milk, unbroken rice, and water combined, with nine jewels and gold —

children.text: śaṅkhasthaṃ pratigṛhṇātu arghaṃ dattaṃ mayā mudā || 53 ||
children.translated_text: Placed in a conch, may [the Lord] accept the <s>argha</s> offered by me with joy — ‖ 53 ‖
Silken garments, divine robes, O Great Radiant One —
Variegated with many colors, may [the Lord] accept them and be delighted — ‖ 54 ‖
Sandal paste born from the <s>Malaya</s> mountains, musk, saffron, and the like,
<s>Śaileya</s> (lichen perfume) and camphor — may they be accepted with approval — ‖ 55 ‖
Aquatic and terrestrial, divine, strung together in five colors,
Endowed with sweet fragrance and perfume — may [the Lord] accept these flowers and be delighted — ‖ 56 ‖
This incense, satisfying to the sense of smell, well-prepared with divine fragrances,
Is offered for your pleasure — may it be accepted, O you who are affectionate to devotees — ‖ 57 ‖
This lamp dispels darkness, the destroyer of all obscurity,
Blazing with ghee and oil — offered by me, may it be accepted — ‖ 58 ‖

children.text: annaṃ caturvidhaṃ nātha rasānāṃ ṣaḍvidhaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: Food of four kinds, O Lord, and flavors of six kinds as well —

children.text: ghṛtādyān śarkarāhārān bhuñjatāṃ ca sukhaṃ mama || 59 ||
children.translated_text: Consisting of ghee and other sweet preparations — may you eat for my happiness — ‖ 59 ‖
Various delightful fruits, cocoons and so forth,
Stems, roots, leaves, and the like — accept them and be pleased — ‖ 60 ‖
Betel leaf combined with areca nut, camphor that is spotless,
And assemblages of divine herbs — may they be accepted, with the wish for your benefit — ‖ 61 ‖
Parched grain, unbroken rice, fruits, offerings, <s>dūrvā</s> grass, and jasmine buds — with devotion,
These have been cast by me for you — accept them, O benevolent one — ‖ 62 ‖
Parasols made of gold and other [materials], banners of various kinds,
And flags of every sort — may the <s>Jina</s> (Victor) accept them and be delighted — ‖ 63 ‖

children.text: dhīmān pujāṃ tathā kṛtva stotram evaṃ ca kārayet /
children.translated_text: The wise one, having performed the worship thus, should have the hymn recited.
For the purpose of pleasing the Lord of <s>Jinas</s>, one should perform the circumambulation — ‖ 64 ‖
The <s>caitya</s> that is the embodiment of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, the form of all worlds,
The abode of all <s>Buddhas</s> — I bow to the <s>Jina</s> relic — ‖ 65 ‖
Homage to you, O <s>Jina</s> relics, manifest with [your] divine play.
The bliss of the community of the three vehicles — I ever take refuge in you — ‖ 66 ‖

children.text: jinajaṃ sakalasthaṃ ca puṇyakṣetraṃ namāmy aham /
children.translated_text: Born of the <s>Jina</s>, present everywhere, the field of merit — I bow.
The giver of desired objects for the happiness of pure people — ‖ 67 ‖
I bow to the best of sages, the bestower of auspicious goals,
The destroyer of the fears of beings, the Lord of the World, the Great Sovereign — ‖ 68 ‖
All the deities dwelling in all worlds, assembled in the <s>Jina</s>'s <s>maṇḍala</s> —

children.text: dadyāt tebhyo baliṃ tuṣṭyā pūjābhaktyarcanair ataḥ || 69 ||
children.translated_text: One should offer <s>bali</s> (oblations) to them with satisfaction, through worship, devotion, and homage — ‖ 69 ‖

children.text:
{CD add the following after vs. 69
śaucasobhanādikaṃ kṛtvā vratinaḥ
maurikuṇḍalasarvābharaṇagāṃgopayādivastra śobhayen mālāpuṣpa
lohayen maṇḍalī prajvālayen vistareṇopaḍoṣita
gandhāya te 'grata dhūpayet sarvapāpaprasamanaṃ bhavati}
children.translated_text: [Manuscript addition: Having performed purification, adornment, and the like, the vow-observers should be adorned with earrings, all ornaments, garments of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the like, flower garlands; one should illuminate the <s>maṇḍala</s>; having made elaborate preparations, one should offer incense before them; it becomes the pacification of all sins.]
With many auspicious musical instruments, with a parasol, vermilion, and vessels,

children.text: ācāryaḥ svastivākyaiś ca kārayec ca mahotsavam || 70 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>ācārya</s> (preceptor), with benedictory verses, should conduct the great festival — ‖ 70 ‖
On the full moon of <s>Aśvinī</s>, on a Sunday,
When conjoined with the <s>Āyuṣmatī</s> <s>yoga</s> — this is especially auspicious — ‖ 71 ‖

children.text: yaḥ prakuryād vrataṃ tasmin vipulaṃ bhogam āpnuyāt /
children.translated_text: Whoever performs the vow on that [day] obtains abundant enjoyment.
In the next world, having attained happiness, [one goes] to the world of the <s>Jinas</s>, O King — ‖ 72 ‖

children.text: śṛṇu rājan mahābhāga vakṣye pūjāphalaṃ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Listen, O King of great fortune; I shall speak again of the fruit of worship.

children.text: yena saṃsthāpitaṃ caityaṃ vītaśoko bhaved asau /
children.translated_text: By whom a <s>caitya</s> has been established — that person becomes free from sorrow,
Released from delusion and illusion, untouched by the three impurities — ‖ 73 ‖
Those who bathe the image of the <s>Jina</s>'s <s>caitya</s> with the five nectars, with sandal paste and fragrances,
With the perfumed waters of the heavenly <s>Mandākinī</s> river — they enjoy pleasures with celestial nymphs (<s>apsarases</s>) — ‖ 74 ‖

children.text: ye dhūpayanti kṣaṇam atra lokāḥ śokā na teṣāṃ prabhavanti jātu /
children.translated_text: Those people who offer incense here even for a moment — sorrows never befall them.
With lotus-feet worshipped by gods and demons, with bodies adorned by fragrant garlands and garments — ‖ 75 ‖

children.text: sugandham asmā upaḍhaukayanti prasannacittā manujā ajasram /
children.translated_text: Those people who, with serene minds, continually present fragrances to this [<s>caitya</s>] —
They become beings of fragrant bodies, radiant as the sun, in the highest worlds — ‖ 76 ‖

children.text: ye kuṅkumādyai racitaṃ suvastraṃ dadanti ye caityatathāgatebhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who give fine garments adorned with saffron and the like to the <s>caityas</s> and <s>Tathāgatas</s> —

children.text: śītārtiduḥkhaṃ na hi jātu teṣāṃ taddhetutaḥ koṣaviśālasāram || 77 ||
children.translated_text: The suffering of cold never [touches] them; by that cause they obtain great treasuries of wealth — ‖ 77 ‖
All flowers, aquatic and terrestrial — white, red, dark blue, beautiful yellow, and black —
[Offered] to <s>Samantabhadra</s> of vast lineage — from the gift, health and happiness arise — ‖ 78 ‖

children.text: śraddhāratā ye manujā udārair mālāsugandhair bahupuṣpayuktaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Those people who, delighting in faith, with magnificent garlands and fragrances joined with many flowers,

children.text: caranti pūjāṃ bahubhaktitas te samastasaukhyāni labhanti loke || 79 ||
children.translated_text: Perform worship with great devotion — they obtain all happiness in this world — ‖ 79 ‖
Delightful to the eye, possessing treasuries of many jewels, with lotus-feet worshipped by kings,
With the net of delusion destroyed by the lamp of wisdom — [such become] those who arrange garlands of lamps for the <s>Buddha</s> — ‖ 80 ‖

children.text: naivedyam asmai pradadāti loke yo bhaktiyuktaḥ surasaṃ sugandhim /
children.translated_text: Whoever, endowed with devotion, offers delicious and fragrant food to this [<s>caitya</s>] in this world —
[That person becomes] powerful, distinguished, a crest-jewel among the circles of men, with feet worshipped [by kings], attended by rulers — ‖ 81 ‖
Having given fruits, roots, and the like at <s>caityas</s>, with a mind of devotion,

children.text: yatheṣṭaṃ phalam āpnoti nirogī sukhavān sadā || 82 ||
children.translated_text: One obtains the desired fruit, and is ever healthy and happy — ‖ 82 ‖
Freed from diseases and other powerful causes of suffering, with gentle faces, of beautiful complexion like gold,

children.text: rājyaṃ hi yad vigatakaṇṭakam āpnuvanti bhaiṣajyadānavidhinā tad uśanti caitye || 83 ||
children.translated_text: They obtain a kingdom free from thorns [of enemies] — those who offer medicines at the <s>caitya</s> according to the proper rite — ‖ 83 ‖
Having given betel leaf and the like, one becomes beautiful, happy, and pure.
Captivating as a divine maiden, one attains royal splendor — ‖ 84 ‖

children.text: vitānam uccair vitanoti caitye dhanyas triloke paripūjanīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: One who spreads a canopy on high at the <s>caitya</s> — fortunate, worthy of worship in the three worlds,
Of vast lineage, to be guarded for [one's] virtues, born with a body of great radiance — ‖ 85 ‖

children.text: dhvajān patākān abhiropayanti ye caityabimbe khalu bhaktiyuktāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who raise banners and flags upon the image of the <s>caitya</s>, endowed with devotion —

children.text: mahīśvarās te jitaduṣṭasaṃghā bhavanti nāthā divi bhūtale ca || 86 ||
children.translated_text: They become lords of the earth, having conquered hostile hosts, protectors in heaven and on earth — ‖ 86 ‖

children.text: chattrāṇi nānāmaṇibhir mahārhaiḥ saṃpādayanty āttamanā dadanti /
children.translated_text: Those who produce and give parasols adorned with various precious jewels, with joyful minds,
At <s>caityas</s> — they become honored by assemblies of earthly rulers, endowed with prosperity, devoted to the <s>Dharma</s> — ‖ 87 ‖
With <s>vīṇās</s> and the like, with bells, <s>mṛdaṅga</s> drums, and instruments, with horns, conches, and other divine sounds —

children.text: saṃghoṣaṇāṃ ye vitaranti caitye te 'bhijñayā pañcabhir āśrayante || 88 ||
children.translated_text: Those who make music at the <s>caitya</s> — they become endowed with the five supernatural knowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) — ‖ 88 ‖
With songs of great enthusiasm, with beautiful and pleasing voices, at the <s>Jina</s>'s [shrine] —

children.text: nṛtyaṃ ca kārayen nityaṃ kuryāc ca divyaghoṣaṇām || 89 ||
children.translated_text: One should always have dance performed and make divine proclamations — ‖ 89 ‖

children.text: te narāḥ susvarā bhonti sundarā divi bhūtale /
children.translated_text: Those people become sweet-voiced, beautiful in heaven and on earth.
Possessed of divine hearing, of great wisdom, they always hear pleasing sounds — ‖ 90 ‖
Having performed dance, song, and the like at the <s>caitya</s> image in the <s>Jina</s>'s abode —

children.text: vandyamānāḥ sugotrāś ca niṣpāpāś ca bahuśrutāḥ || 91 ||
children.translated_text: [They become] honored, of noble family, sinless, and learned in many things — ‖ 91 ‖
Long-lived, thousand-eyed, free from calamities, repositories of virtues,
With limbs freed from planetary afflictions and diseases — they become auspicious ones — ‖ 92 ‖
For the terror of evil beings and for the protection of the <s>Jina</s>'s abode,
Those who stand with weapons in hand, endowed with devotion to the <s>Jina</s> — ‖ 93 ‖
They become long-lived, free from disease, endowed with sons and grandsons,

children.text: bhāgyavanto dhanāḍhyāś ca gacchanty ante jinālayam || 94 ||
children.translated_text: Fortunate, wealthy, and at the end they go to the abode of the <s>Jinas</s> — ‖ 94 ‖
One who, with devotion, casts <s>dūrvā</s> grass, jasmine buds, unbroken rice, flowers, and parched grain
At <s>Jina</s> <s>caityas</s>, uttering benedictory verses — ‖ 95 ‖
One never experiences an unfortunate rebirth; [one becomes] of noble family, a delight to the world,
A master of all learning, worthy of homage — and at the end attains liberation — ‖ 96 ‖
Those who, by giving gems, pearls, jewels, diamonds, gold, silver, fine gold, and other metals —

children.text: vinaṣṭaśokāḥ subhagāḥ suvaṃśāḥ pūrṇendriyāḥ pūrṇamanorathāḥ syuḥ || 97 ||
children.translated_text: Free from sorrow, fortunate, of noble lineage, with complete faculties, they shall have all their desires fulfilled.

children.text: ye śuddhacittāḥ stutim ācaranti gadyātmikāṃ padyamayīṃ vicitrām /
children.translated_text: Those who with pure hearts perform praise, both in prose and in varied verse,

children.text: te śabdasaṃghān bahuvādyajātān śṛṇvanti gītān surabhāminīnām || 98 ||
children.translated_text: they hear the multitudes of sounds, many kinds of music, and the songs of celestial women.

children.text: yāvatī bhūmir ākrāntā hy adhaḥ kāñcanacakrataḥ /
children.translated_text: As much earth as is covered below by the golden wheel,
thousands of <s>yojanas</s> (leagues) are declared in heaps.
As many grains of sand as are there, that many times by count
one becomes a king, a lord of heroes, a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal sovereign) on the earth.

children.text: ye jātamātrāḥ prabhutāṃ prayānti śreṣṭhīkule janma sadaiva yeṣām /
children.translated_text: Those who from birth itself attain sovereignty, whose birth is always in the family of a <s>śreṣṭhin</s> (guild-master),

children.text: hastyaśvayānaiś ca paribhramanti kṛtvātra te caityavarapraṇāmam || 101 ||
children.translated_text: and who travel about on elephants, horses, and vehicles — they have performed obeisance to the excellent <s>caitya</s> (sacred shrine) here.

children.text: akāra-m-ādyakṣaramantrarājair balyūpahāraṃ khalu yo hi dadyāt /
children.translated_text: He who offers <s>bali</s> (ritual oblation) with the king of <s>mantras</s> beginning with the syllable 'a',

children.text: tasmai sudevāḥ sagaṇāḥ sutṛptā dāsyanti satkarmaphalābhilāṣam || 102 ||
children.translated_text: to him the well-pleased <s>devas</s> (gods) together with their retinues will grant the desired fruit of good <s>karma</s> (action).
Those who apply a plaster of lime upon it, they become free from disease, sorrow, and the like in body,

children.text: dhaneśvarā dīrghatarāyuṣas te narāmarāṇāṃ subhagā bhavanti || 103 ||
children.translated_text: lords of wealth, of exceedingly long life, and they become fortunate among men and gods.

children.text: ye buddham uddiśya mahānti nityaṃ kurvanti mṛdgomayalepanāni /
children.translated_text: Those who, dedicating their service to the <s>Buddha</s>, constantly perform great applications of clay and cow-dung,

children.text: bhaktyā suśuddhā jalamaṇḍalaṃ vā labhanti te rājabalaṃ subhāgyāḥ || 104 ||
children.translated_text: or with devotion purely offer a <s>jalamaṇḍala</s> (water-circle offering) — they, being fortunate, obtain royal power.

children.text: stūpāṅgaṇaṃ dhātuvaraṃ vihāraṃ ye śodhayantīha narāḥ prayatnaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Those people who with effort cleanse the courtyard of the <s>stūpa</s>, the excellent relic-shrine, and the <s>vihāra</s> (monastery),

children.text: nirmālyam ebhyaś ca samuddharanti te hemavarṇāḥ sudṛśo bhavanti || 105 ||
children.translated_text: and who remove the withered offerings from these — they become golden-complexioned and beautiful to behold.

children.text: pradakṣiṇāṃ ye vitaranti tasmin bhavanti jātismaralābhinas te /
children.translated_text: Those who perform <s>pradakṣiṇā</s> (circumambulation) around it obtain the attainment of <s>jātismara</s> (remembrance of past lives),
become golden-complexioned, blessed with many sons and grandsons, and are worshipped by assemblies of men, gods, and <s>Nāthas</s> (lords).
Even one who performs <s>pradakṣiṇā</s> (circumambulation) of a <s>Jina</s>-temple (temple of the Conqueror) out of laziness,
at every step obtains the fruit of donating one <s>karṣa</s> (a weight-measure) of gold.
The worship is proper for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, and also <s>Śūdras</s>;
but for those of castes lower than these, there is no entitlement to worship.
One should worship with incense, flowers, and the twice-born ... ;
the worship with incense and flowers by the twice-born is especially prescribed.
For kings, the lowering of the umbrella is prescribed; for <s>Vaiśyas</s>, the offering of food;
and for <s>Śūdras</s>, the offering of banners, flags, and cloths is declared.
Goldsmiths, ironsmiths, bronze-workers, farmers, and the like —
for these, the worship of the supreme <s>caitya</s> (sacred shrine) is to be done by hand.
Rice-sellers, vegetable-sellers, and those engaged in buying and selling —
by these, the goods of their own trade should be offered with devotion.
Oil-pressers, incense-sellers, meat-sellers, and liquor-sellers —
by these, lamps should be offered according to the measure of their family <s>dharma</s> (duty).

children.text: carmakāraś ca mātaṅgo niyogī rajako dhvajī /
children.translated_text: Leather-workers, <s>Mātaṅgas</s> (outcaste people), servants, washermen, and flag-bearers —

children.text: etaiś ca dūrataḥ sthitvā vandanīyo jinālayaḥ || 114 ||
children.translated_text: by these, standing from a distance, the <s>Jina</s>-temple (temple of the Conqueror) should be saluted.
Thus by the thirty-six castes, each following the conduct of their own family occupation,

children.text: anyaiś ca vividhair nityaṃ pūjyo mānyo jinālayaḥ || 115 ||
children.translated_text: and by others of various kinds, the <s>Jina</s>-temple should always be worshipped and honored.
For those who have no deviation from the vow in worshipping the supreme <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror),
having performed <s>pradakṣiṇā</s> (circumambulation), the temple should be saluted with one's own devotion.

children.text: evaṃ bhūyaś cared dharmī vratarājam aharniśam /
children.translated_text: Thus should the righteous person observe even more the king of vows, day and night;

children.text: tasya puṇyaṃ yathā proktaṃ kuṣṭhavyādhikṣayaṃ vrajet || 117 ||
children.translated_text: the merit thereof, as declared, shall destroy leprosy, disease, and consumption.
Even the five <s>ānantarya</s>-sins (sins of immediate retribution) shall be destroyed, there is no doubt;
how much more then other sins, even those committed in previous births!

children.text: na hī sa vidyate rājan sarvatra bhuvaneṣv api /
children.translated_text: There exists not, O King, anywhere in all the worlds,
anyone who could render otherwise the merit of the <s>ahorātravrata</s> (day-and-night vow).

children.text: śravād api haret pāpaṃ darśanāt puṇyam āpnuyāt /
children.translated_text: Even by hearing about it, sin is removed; by seeing it, merit is obtained;

children.text: anumodāt tathā caivaṃ vratināṃ tu kim ucyate || 120 ||
children.translated_text: likewise by rejoicing in it — so what then need be said of those who actually observe the vow?
The wise one, having divided the merit of those observing the vow into seven parts,

children.text: ekabhāgaṃ labhed rājā caikaṃ tu sārathījanaḥ /
children.translated_text: one part the king obtains, and one part the charioteer-folk obtain,

children.text: sarvasattvasya caikaṃ hi tac cheṣaṃ labhate vratī || 121 ||
children.translated_text: and one part is for all beings — the remainder the vow-observer obtains.

children.text: iti śrutvā guror vākyam indrapṛṣṭo mahāprabhuḥ //
children.translated_text: Having heard this word of the guru, <s>Indrapṛṣṭha</s>, the great lord,
then for the benefit of all beings, undertook to perform the vow.
Going to the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, as per the word of <s>Vasubandhu</s>,
having established a <s>vihāra</s> (monastery) and a <s>caityarāja</s> (supreme sacred shrine), a <s>Jina</s>-temple,

children.text: saṃghabhojyaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā yayau svargaṃ janaiḥ sudhīḥ || 123 ||
children.translated_text: and having then made a feast for the <s>Saṃgha</s> (monastic community), the wise one went to heaven together with the people.
Then the <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One):

children.text: bhagavan muniśārdūla punar vaktuṃ tvam arhasi /
children.translated_text: "O <s>Bhagavān</s>, O tiger among sages, please speak again —

children.text: kena kena purā nātha vratarājam idaṃ kṛtam || 124 ||
children.translated_text: by whom, by whom in the past, O Lord, was this king of vows performed?"
The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) said:
"In ancient times, in the heavens, the <s>ahorātravrata</s> (day-and-night vow) was performed by <s>Śakra</s>,
who, upholding the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), worshipped the <s>caityarāja</s> (supreme sacred shrine),
always performing <s>pradakṣiṇā</s> (circumambulation) according to the prescribed rites, with great festivals.

children.text: pātāle ca purā vīro daityendro balavān abhūt /
children.translated_text: And in the <s>Pātāla</s> (netherworld), in ancient times, there was a powerful hero, a lord of <s>Daityas</s> (demons),
named <s>Nirghoṣadamana</s>, crusher of gods and <s>Asuras</s> (anti-gods).
Having expelled <s>Indra</s> from heaven and having subjugated the earth,
with the help of the <s>Asuras</s>, he brought the three worlds under his control.
Going to the circle of the earth, he went to the city of <s>Maghavat</s> (Indra),
and at the great site of <s>Indrapṛṣṭha</s>, where the image of the deity stood,
having performed five circumambulations, he became established in the perfection of <s>Prajñā</s> (wisdom).

children.text: pātāleṣu punar gatvā so 'carat tad vratottamam /
children.translated_text: Going again to the <s>Pātāla</s> (netherworlds), he practiced that supreme vow;

children.text: nāginyo nāgarājāś ca pātāleṣv acaraṃs tathā || 129 ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Nāginīs</s> (serpent-princesses) and <s>Nāgarājas</s> (serpent-kings) in the netherworlds practiced it likewise.
By the <s>Nāgas</s> (serpent-beings), with ornaments of their hoods, a shrine fashioned for the lord of <s>Devas</s> and <s>Nāgas</s>
was worshipped constantly with devotion according to the proper rites, the supreme <s>caitya</s> (sacred shrine).
And in ancient times, seven <s>Ṛṣis</s> (sages), at a shrine established near a body of water,
worshipped it, containing relics of the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror), with proper rites, being learned.
The <s>Nāginīs</s> (serpent-princesses), blinded by the pride of their venom, while the <s>Jina</s>-temple was being worshipped,
caused the sages to be tormented with burning poisonous embers.

children.text: tatas taiḥ śāpitā evaṃ nāginyaḥ śambukāḥ khalu /
children.translated_text: Then, cursed by those sages, those <s>Nāginīs</s> indeed became snails:
'Be you snails for seven births, and then again become servants of the <s>caitya</s> (sacred shrine)!'

children.text: tataś cānte punaḥ prāpya mānuṣyaṃ puṇyabhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Then at the end of that period, having again obtained human birth through the power of merit,

children.text: eṣā sā nāyakā yā tu dharmadakṣaṃ patiṃ labhet || 134 ||
children.translated_text: this is that leader who obtained <s>Dharmadakṣa</s> as her husband.

children.text: tatas ta vañcitāḥ sarvāḥ śambukā dharmamānasāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then all those cursed ones became snails with minds inclined toward <s>dharma</s> (righteousness),
and they performed auspicious circumambulations, meditating upon the <s>Jina</s>-temple.
Then, by the power of their merit, the seven princesses, now celestial maidens,

children.text: bhūtā rājasutā dhanyāḥ prālabhan paramaṃ padam || 136 ||
children.translated_text: became blessed daughters of kings and attained the highest state.
Among them, one vow-observer, named <s>Dharmadakṣapativratā</s> (she devoted to her husband Dharmadakṣa),
by the power of her merit, <s>Dharmadakṣa</s> obtained the vow.
<s>Dharmadakṣa</s>, the great king, observing the vow according to the prescribed rites,
the righteous sovereign together with his wife attained <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (the Pure Land of Bliss).

children.text: ity evaṃ bhikṣavo jñātvā vratānāṃ vratam uttamam /
children.translated_text: Thus, O <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), having understood this, the supreme among vows,
worship of the <s>caitya</s> (sacred shrine) should always be performed, with the practice of the merit of the vow.
There is no merit equal to the <s>caitya</s>-vow (sacred shrine vow) in the three worlds, truly;

children.text: tasmāc caityaḥ sadā vandyaḥ pūjanīyaḥ prayatnataḥ || 140 ||
children.translated_text: therefore the <s>caitya</s> (sacred shrine) should always be saluted and worshipped with effort.
Thus ends the <s>Ahorātravratakathā</s> (Story of the Day-and-Night Vow).
